description: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by country or region of origin, as presented in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning 2012 to 2022. Each year features a grouped set of colored bars corresponding to six categories: “Other” (blue), “UK” (red), “USA” (orange), “IT” (purple), “IN” (green), and “DE” (brown), as indicated in the legend. In early years (2012–2015), datasets are sparse, mostly from the USA and “Other” categories. From 2016 onward, dataset counts increase significantly, with “Other” consistently having the highest number of datasets each year, peaking at over 100 in 2021. The USA follows as the second most frequent source, with values reaching nearly 50 in 2021. The UK, IN, IT, and DE show more modest and variable contributions, with the UK and IN occasionally exceeding 10 datasets in peak years (e.g., UK in 2020 and 2021, IN in 2021). The 2022 data show a decline across most categories, with “Other” still leading at approximately 30 datasets. No bars are shaded or annotated beyond their color-coded category, and the bars are not sorted within each year — they maintain a fixed order as per the legend. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of “Other” and “USA” in dataset production over time, while also highlighting the growing but uneven global contribution to hateful communication research.
